chunks.title: Explosion/Fire/Shock Hazard Precautions
chunks.content: Never mix chlorine bleach with ammonia or acids like vinegar as it can produce lethal gas; hydrogen gas can build up in unused hot water systems and is explosive, so run hot taps before use after long idle periods.

scenarios.condition: Gas leak detected (propane, LP gas, etc.)
steps: Do not operate this or any other appliance
Open a window or door to ventilate the area immediately
Leave the area and contact your gas supplier

scenarios.condition: Hot water system unused for two weeks or more
steps: Turn on all hot water faucets before using the appliance
Let water flow from each faucet for several minutes to release accumulated hydrogen gas
Do not smoke or use an open flame during this process
Never mix chlorine bleach with ammonia, vinegar, or rust/scale remover
Follow package directions for all laundry products
If mixed accidentally, ventilate the area immediately and leave the area

chunks.title: Electrical Shock and Grounding Hazards
chunks.content: The washer must be properly grounded via a 3-prong outlet; never cut the ground prong, use an adapter, or extension cord, and never touch the appliance or cord with wet hands.

scenarios.condition: Cord or plug is damaged, worn, or the appliance was submerged
steps: Contact LG Customer Information Center or a qualified electrician before resuming use

chunks.title: Steam Cycle Burn Warning
chunks.content: During steam cycles the door surface becomes very hot; never touch the door or attempt to override the door lock or reach inside during a steam cycle as steam can cause severe burns.

chunks.title: Moving Parts and Reaching Into Drum
chunks.content: Never reach into the washer while the tub, drum, or interior parts are moving; press Start/Pause and wait for a complete stop before loading, unloading, or adding items.

chunks.title: Waterproof Items Must Use Bedding Cycle
chunks.content: Waterproof or water-resistant items (raincoats, mattress covers, plastic mats) must only be washed on the Bedding cycle with low spin, otherwise abnormal vibration may damage the washer, clothes, or surroundings.

chunks.title: Fire Hazard from Chemicals and Fabrics
chunks.content: Never wash or add items previously exposed to gasoline, dry-cleaning solvents, or cooking oil, and never place oily/greasy clothing or flammable materials on or in the washer, as vapors could ignite or explode.

chunks.title: Installation Electrical & Environmental Requirements
chunks.content: The washer must be installed by qualified personnel on a firm level floor, away from freezing temperatures or humid/outdoor spaces, and moving/installing requires two or more people.

chunks.title: Product Specifications
chunks.content: 120 VAC @ 60Hz electrical requirement, 20-120 psi water pressure, dimensions 27"W x 30 1/4"D x 39"H, net weight 187.4 lb, max spin speed 1300 RPM.

chunks.title: Installation Overview and Location Selection
chunks.content: Install on a solid, level floor free of slope over 1 inch, keep the power outlet within 60 inches, maintain 1 inch side clearance and 4 inches rear clearance, and avoid carpet or platforms.

chunks.title: Unpack and Remove Shipping Bolts
chunks.content: Lift the washer off the foam base ensuring the tub support isn't stuck to the bottom, use the included wrench to loosen and remove all four shipping bolts counterclockwise, then install the hole caps.

chunks.title: Connect Water Supply Lines
chunks.content: Inspect hose rubber seals, hand-tighten hoses to hot/cold faucets (red=hot, blue=cold) plus 2/3 turn with pliers, flush hoses into a bucket, then attach to the washer's rear inlets and check for leaks.

chunks.title: Connect the Drain Hose
chunks.content: Clip the elbow bracket within 4 inches of the drain hose end, then insert into a standpipe or hang over a laundry tub edge, and secure with the included tie strap.

chunks.title: Level the Washer
chunks.content: Position the washer, adjust the lower leveling feet to raise/lower until level (max 1 inch slope), tighten the locknuts, then rock the washer to confirm it doesn't wobble; use non-skid pads on slippery floors.

chunks.title: Connect Power and Test the Washer
chunks.content: Plug into a grounded 120-VAC 3-prong outlet, then run a test cycle by loading 6 lb of laundry, pressing Power, selecting Rinse+Spin, and pressing Start/Pause to verify fill, balance, and drain.

chunks.title: Basic Washer Operation Sequence
chunks.content: Sort and load laundry, add HE detergent/bleach/softener to the dispenser, press Power, turn the Cycle Selector Knob to choose a cycle, adjust settings if desired, then press Start/Pause to begin; remove laundry promptly at cycle end.

chunks.title: Sorting Laundry for Best Results
chunks.content: Sort laundry by color, soil level, fabric type, and lint type to avoid poor wash performance, dye transfer, or linting; do not tightly pack the drum and use the Bedding cycle for pillows/comforters.

chunks.title: Loading the Dispenser Drawer
chunks.content: Open the drawer and add liquid detergent (with cup in place) or powdered detergent (cup removed) to the main compartment, bleach to its compartment, and softener to its compartment; close the drawer slowly to avoid premature dispensing.

chunks.title: HE Detergent Use Guidelines
chunks.content: Use only High-Efficiency (HE) detergent and less than half the manufacturer's recommended maximum amount; overuse causes oversudsing, poor rinsing, and residue buildup that contributes to odors.

chunks.title: Control Panel Overview
chunks.content: The control panel includes Power On/Off, Cycle Selector Knob, Start/Pause, cycle modifier buttons (Temp., Spin, Soil, Signal), special cycle/option buttons, and a time/status display.

chunks.title: Wash Cycle Guide
chunks.content: Cycle options include Normal, Bright Whites, Perm.Press, Delicates, Towels, Sportswear, Bedding, Speed Wash, Heavy Duty, Sanitary, Allergiene, Tub Clean, and Downloaded, each with distinct temp/spin/soil defaults.

chunks.title: Cycle Modifier Buttons: Temp, Spin, Soil, Signal
chunks.content: Use Temp. to select wash/rinse temperature, Spin to set extraction speed (also activates Drain+Spin), Soil to adjust cycle time/wash action for soil level, and Signal to adjust melody/button volume.

chunks.title: Special Options: Steam, Fresh Care, Pre Wash, Delay Wash
chunks.content: Steam boosts cleaning with hot steam (not for delicates); Fresh Care tumbles the load periodically up to 19 hours after cycle end to prevent wrinkles; Pre Wash adds a 15-minute soak for heavily soiled items; Delay Wash delays start up to 19 hours.

chunks.title: Add Garments Mid-Cycle
chunks.content: Press Add Garments to pause and unlock the door (if temperature/water level allow), add or remove items, close the door, then press Start/Pause to resume; disabled during Tub Clean or Spin for safety.

chunks.title: Turbo Wash, Cold Wash, Extra Rinse, Rinse+Spin, Control Lock
chunks.content: Turbo Wash shortens cycle time; Cold Wash saves energy using cooler water with longer wash times; Extra Rinse adds rinses; Rinse+Spin runs a standalone rinse/spin; Control Lock disables all buttons except Power (hold 3 seconds to toggle).

chunks.title: LG SmartThinQ App Setup and Features
chunks.content: Connect a smartphone to the same 2.4GHz Wi-Fi network as the washer, install the SmartThinQ app, and use it for Remote Start, cycle downloads, Tub Clean Coach, Smart Diagnosis, energy monitoring, and push alerts.

chunks.title: Smart Diagnosis via Phone or App
chunks.content: Call the LG Customer Information Center, hold the phone near the Smart Diagnosis icon, press and hold Temp. for 3 seconds to transmit diagnostic tones, or use the Smart Diagnosis feature in the SmartThinQ app directly.

chunks.title: Care After Each Wash
chunks.content: Wipe the door and inside of the door seal to remove moisture after each cycle and leave the door open to dry the drum interior.

chunks.title: Cleaning the Drum with Tub Clean
chunks.content: Add drum cleaner, lime scale remover, liquid bleach, powdered cleaner, or cleaning tablets per compartment instructions, then run the Tub Clean cycle monthly (weekly for 3 weeks if mildew already exists) with the drum empty.

chunks.title: Removing Mineral Buildup
chunks.content: In hard water areas, use a descaler on the drum periodically and always run Tub Clean after descaling; use stainless steel cleaner with a soft cloth for scale spots and never use steel wool.

chunks.title: Clean the Detergent Dispenser Drawer
chunks.content: Slide out and press the disengage button to remove the drawer, remove and rinse the inserts with warm water only, wipe dry, and replace weekly to prevent scale buildup.

chunks.title: Clean the Door Seal
chunks.content: Wearing gloves and goggles, wipe the door seal monthly with a solution of 3/4 cup liquid chlorine bleach diluted in 1 gallon of water, then wipe dry and leave the door open to air dry.

chunks.title: Clean the Water Inlet Filters
chunks.content: Turn off faucets, unscrew hoses, remove filters from the valves, soak in white vinegar or lime scale remover, rinse, reinstall, and flush the hoses before reattaching.

chunks.title: Clean the Drain Pump Filter
chunks.content: Unplug the washer, open the drain pump filter cover, drain remaining water via the hose plug, twist the pump filter counterclockwise to remove and clean it, then reinstall everything in reverse order.

chunks.title: Cold Climate Storage and Winterizing
chunks.content: To store the washer in freezing conditions, drain and disconnect hoses, add 1 gallon of RV antifreeze to the empty drum, run a brief spin/drain cycle to distribute it, then dry and store upright; run a Speed Wash cycle to remove antifreeze before reuse.

chunks.title: Noises You Might Hear
chunks.content: Common noises like spraying, humming, sloshing, and added water are normal operation; rattling, thumping, vibrating, or squeaking usually indicate foreign objects, unbalanced loads, un-leveled feet, or leftover shipping bolts.

rows: Foreign objects in drum or pump
Stop washer, check drum and drain filter
Shipping bolts not removed / not level
Plumbing moves when valves shut off

chunks.title: Operation Problems: Leaks, No Power, No Drain
chunks.content: Water leaks are often caused by loose hose connections, clogged house drains, oversized loads above the drum, or oversudsing; no power issues stem from unplugged cords or tripped breakers.

rows: Check hose position, no more than 5 ft away
Dispenser cover not installed or clogged

chunks.title: Water Fill and Level Issues
chunks.content: Slow filling is usually due to clogged inlet filters, kinked hoses, or low water pressure; low or invisible water in the drum during wash is normal for HE washers and does not indicate a fault.

rows: Water level too low / not visible

chunks.title: Performance Issues: Wrinkling, Staining, Odor
chunks.content: Wrinkling results from delayed unloading or overloading; staining from bleach/softener overfilled or added directly to the drum; odor from unclean door seal, drain filter, or new rubber smell that fades with use.

rows: Remove items as soon as cycle ends
Clean gasket and door seal regularly

chunks.title: Wi-Fi Connection Troubleshooting
chunks.content: Connection failures are usually due to incorrect passwords, mobile data left on, non-2.4GHz routers, or excessive distance from the router; a Wi-Fi repeater can help extend range.

rows: Move router closer or add a Wi-Fi repeater

chunks.title: Error Codes Reference
chunks.content: Error codes like IE (fill), UE (unbalanced), dE (door), OE (drain), tE (control), FE (overfill), PE (sensor), LE (motor), Sud (oversudsing), FF (frozen lines), CL (control lock), and tCL (tub clean needed) each map to specific causes and fixes.

rows: Slow/no water fill; low pressure or clogged filters
Clean inlet filters, check faucets fully open
Close and secure door; call service if persists
Drain hose kinked/clogged or too high
Check hose position and clear clogs
Close faucets, unplug, call for service
Close faucets, unplug, call for service
Let stand 30 min, restart; call service if persists
Hold Control Lock 3 seconds to disable

tasks.title: Remove Shipping Bolts and Hole Caps
tasks.description: Remove the four shipping bolts and retainers before first use and install the plastic hole caps.
tasks.justification: Failing to remove shipping bolts causes severe vibration and permanent internal damage.
tasks.instructions_text: Lift the washer off the foam base. Use the included wrench to turn all four shipping bolts counterclockwise starting with the bottom two, wiggle and pull out the bolt assemblies, then snap the hole caps into the empty holes.

tasks.title: Level the Washer
tasks.description: Adjust the leveling feet so the washer sits flat and stable on the floor.
tasks.justification: An unlevel washer vibrates excessively, causing noise and potential machine malfunction.
tasks.instructions_text: Place a level across the top of the washer, adjust the lower leveling feet by turning them to raise or lower each corner, then tighten the locknuts. Rock the top of the washer to confirm it doesn't wobble; use non-skid pads if the floor is slippery.

re_check_triggers.description: Washer vibrates, walks, or rocks excessively during spin

tasks.title: Connect and Check Water Supply Hoses
tasks.description: Install new inlet hoses correctly to the hot/cold faucets and washer, and check for leaks.
tasks.justification: Old, loose, or incorrectly connected hoses can burst or leak, causing flooding and property damage.
tasks.instructions_text: Connect the blue hose to the cold faucet and red hose to the hot faucet, hand-tighten then add 2/3 turn with pliers. Flush the hoses into a bucket, attach them to the washer's rear inlets, turn faucets on fully, and check both ends for leaks.

re_check_triggers.description: Water pools around the hose connections or under the washer

tasks.title: Connect and Secure Drain Hose
tasks.description: Attach the drain hose to a standpipe or laundry tub using the elbow bracket and tie strap.
tasks.justification: An improperly secured drain hose can come loose and flood the area during draining.
tasks.instructions_text: Clip the elbow bracket within 4 inches of the drain hose end, insert the hose into the standpipe or hang it over the laundry tub edge, then secure it in place with the included tie strap.

re_check_triggers.description: Water leaks or backs up near the drain during a cycle

tasks.title: Verify Grounded Power Connection
tasks.description: Plug the washer into a properly grounded 3-prong 120V outlet.
tasks.justification: Improper grounding creates a risk of electric shock in the event of a malfunction.
tasks.instructions_text: Confirm the outlet is a grounded, 3-prong, 120 VAC 60 Hz outlet located within 60 inches of the washer, and plug the power cord in directly without an adapter or extension cord.

re_check_triggers.description: Sparks, burning smell, or shock felt when touching the washer

tasks.title: Run Initial Test Cycle
tasks.description: Run a test wash cycle after installation to confirm proper fill, balance, and drain.
tasks.justification: Confirms the installation is correct before regular use, preventing leaks or vibration damage later.
tasks.instructions_text: Load about 6 lb of laundry (roughly 6 towels), press Power, select Rinse+Spin, then press Start/Pause. Check that water fills properly, the machine doesn't vibrate excessively, and it drains well during spin.

tasks.title: Run Tub Clean Cycle
tasks.description: Run the Tub Clean cycle monthly to remove detergent buildup, mildew, and residue from the empty drum.
tasks.justification: Skipping this allows residue buildup that leads to mildew, musty odors, and reduced wash performance.
tasks.instructions_text: With the drum empty, add drum cleaner, lime scale remover, or bleach to the appropriate dispenser compartment (or a cleaning tablet directly in the drum), select the Tub Clean cycle, and press Start/Pause. Leave the door open afterward so the drum can dry completely. If mildew or musty smell is already present, run this cycle weekly for three consecutive weeks instead.

supplies.name: Drum cleaner or lime scale remover

tasks.title: Clean the Detergent Dispenser Drawer
tasks.description: Pull out and clean the detergent dispenser drawer and its inserts to remove scale buildup.
tasks.justification: Leftover detergent buildup can clog compartments, preventing proper dispensing and causing residue on clothes.
tasks.instructions_text: Slide the drawer out fully, press the disengage button, and pull it out. Remove the inserts, rinse them and the drawer with warm water only using a soft cloth or brush, wipe dry, and reinstall.

tasks.title: Clean the Door Seal
tasks.description: Wipe down the door seal/gasket monthly with a diluted bleach solution to prevent dirt buildup.
tasks.justification: Neglected door seals accumulate dirt, mold, and odor and small trapped items can damage clothing.
tasks.instructions_text: Wear rubber gloves and goggles, dilute 3/4 cup liquid chlorine bleach in 1 gallon of water, and wipe all around the door seal with a soaked sponge or cloth. Wipe dry afterward and leave the door open to let the seal dry completely. Do not use undiluted bleach as it can damage the seal.

tasks.title: Clean the Water Inlet Filters
tasks.description: Remove and clean the screens inside the water inlet valves to clear sediment or scale.
tasks.justification: Clogged inlet filters cause slow or no water fill and can trigger fill error codes.
tasks.instructions_text: Turn off both faucets, unscrew the hoses from the back of the washer, carefully pull out the filters, and soak them in white vinegar or lime scale remover to remove debris. Rinse thoroughly, press back into place, flush the hoses with a few gallons of water, then reattach.

tasks.title: Clean the Drain Pump Filter
tasks.description: Clean the drain pump filter periodically to prevent clogs from foreign objects.
tasks.justification: A clogged drain pump filter prevents the washer from draining properly and can cause leaks.
tasks.instructions_text: Turn off and unplug the washer, open the drain pump filter cover, unclip the drain hose and remove its plug to drain remaining water into a bucket, then twist the pump filter counterclockwise to remove and clean it. Recap the drain hose, reinsert the filter, and close the cover.

tasks.title: Winterize Washer for Cold Storage
tasks.description: Protect the washer from freeze damage if it will sit unused in an area exposed to freezing temperatures.
tasks.justification: Water left in hoses or the pump can freeze and crack internal components, causing leaks or failure.
tasks.instructions_text: Turn off the water supply, disconnect and drain the hoses, add 1 gallon of nontoxic RV antifreeze to the empty drum, run a brief Spin cycle to circulate and expel it, then unplug, dry the drum, and store the washer upright. Run a full Speed Wash cycle with detergent (no laundry) before resuming normal use. Never use automotive antifreeze.

tasks.title: Wipe Down Washer Exterior and Door
tasks.description: Wipe the door and exterior body of the washer to remove spills and moisture.
tasks.justification: Cosmetic only — prevents spill residue from damaging the finish and keeps the machine looking clean.
tasks.instructions_text: Wipe spills immediately with a damp cloth, then dry with a soft cloth. Clean the door inside and out with a damp cloth and dry with a soft cloth. Do not use volatile chemicals, abrasive cleaners, or sharp objects on the surface or display.

weekly.title: Weekly Cleaning
steps: Pull out and clean the detergent dispenser drawer and inserts with warm water
Wipe the door and door seal dry after each wash and leave the door open to air the drum

deep_clean.title: Monthly Deep Clean
steps: Run the Tub Clean cycle with the drum empty using drum cleaner, bleach, or a cleaning tablet
Wipe the door seal with a diluted bleach solution (3/4 cup bleach to 1 gallon water) and let it air dry
Clean the water inlet filters by soaking in white vinegar or descaler if fill is slow
Clean the drain pump filter if drainage is slow or noisy
Remove mineral/lime buildup from the drum with a descaler, then run Tub Clean again
supplies: Drum cleaner or lime scale remover

warranty.coverage: LG covers parts and labor for internal/functional defects for 1 year from original retail purchase; the stainless steel drum is covered for parts only for 3 years; the direct drive motor (stator, rotor, hall sensor) is covered for parts only for 10 years, with labor charged after year one.
exclusions: Service trips for delivery, pickup, installation, or instruction
Damage from power failures or inadequate electrical service
Damage from leaky/frozen pipes or inadequate water/air supply
Damage from corrosive atmosphere or misuse contrary to owner's manual
Damage from accidents, pests, lightning, fire, floods, acts of God
Damage from unauthorized modification or improper installation
Damage from incorrect electrical current/voltage or unapproved accessories
Cosmetic transport damage not reported within 1 week of delivery
Costs of removing the unit from the home for repair
